topics.title: Responsive Design and Mobile-first
topics.summary: Viewport meta, fluid layouts, mobile-first workflow and modern responsive patterns.
topics.description:
**Responsive design** means one codebase that adapts to every screen size. It rests on three pillars: flexible layouts, flexible media and media queries.

### 1. The viewport meta tag
```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
```
Without it, phones render the page at ~980px and shrink it.

### 2. Mobile-first workflow
Write the **small-screen styles first** with no query, then add enhancements with `min-width` queries:

```css
.layout { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }               /* mobile: 1 column */
@media (min-width: 768px)  { .layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; } }
@media (min-width: 1100px) { .layout { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); } }
```

Benefits: lighter CSS for phones, simpler overrides, forces focus on content.

### 3. Flexible building blocks
- Widths in `%`, `fr`, `min()`, `max-width` instead of fixed px.
- Images: `max-width: 100%; height: auto;`.
- Typography with `rem` and `clamp()`.
- Grid `auto-fit/minmax` and Flexbox `wrap` for self-adjusting layouts.

### 4. Viewport units
`vw`, `vh`, `dvh` (dynamic - adjusts when mobile toolbars appear), `svh` (small), `lvh` (large). Use `min-height: 100dvh;` for full-screen sections.

### 5. Touch and spacing
- Tap targets at least **44x44px**.
- Do not rely on `:hover` for essential actions.
- Use `@media (hover: hover)` for hover-only effects.

### Testing
Use DevTools device mode, real phones, and resize slowly to find where the layout breaks.
keyPoints: Always include the viewport meta tag
Mobile-first = base styles for small screens + min-width queries
Prefer fluid units (%, fr, rem, clamp) to fixed px
Use dvh for mobile full-height sections
Tap targets >= 44px; do not depend on hover
pitfalls: Desktop-first max-width overrides that become very long
100vh sections cut by mobile browser toolbars

The container is fluid up to 640px and centered, with side padding that never touches the edge.

interview.a: Designing and writing base CSS for small screens first, then progressively enhancing for larger screens with min-width media queries.

interview.q: Why is the viewport meta tag needed?
interview.a: It tells mobile browsers to use the device width as layout width and a 1:1 initial scale; otherwise pages are rendered as a zoomed-out desktop layout.

interview.q: What problem do dvh units solve?
interview.a: On mobile, 100vh ignores the collapsing address bar and may overflow; dvh follows the actual visible viewport.

topics.title: calc(), min(), max() and clamp()
topics.summary: Math functions for fluid typography, flexible containers and mixed units.
topics.description:
CSS has built-in math functions that evaluate in the browser.

### calc()
Mix units: `width: calc(100% - 240px);`, `padding: calc(1rem + 2vw);`, `height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-h));`. Operators need spaces around `+` and `-` (not `*` or `/`).

### min() and max()
- `min(100%, 600px)` -> the smaller value: a width that never exceeds 600px (like max-width).
- `max(16px, 2vw)` -> the larger value: a lower bound.

### clamp(min, preferred, max)
Value that scales with the viewport but never goes below min nor above max:

```css
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1rem + 3vw, 3.5rem); }
.container { width: clamp(320px, 90%, 1200px); }
.section { padding-block: clamp(2rem, 6vw, 6rem); }
```

Fluid type means **no media queries** for headings.

### Accessibility note
Keep a `rem` part in the preferred value (`1rem + 3vw`). Pure `vw` ignores user zoom and fails WCAG.

### Useful combos
- Full-bleed + centered content: `padding-inline: max(1rem, (100% - 1100px) / 2);`
- Scale spacing with custom properties: `--space: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem);`

### Where they work
Any property that takes a length, percentage, number or angle. They can nest: `clamp(1rem, calc(0.5rem + 2vw), 2rem)` (inner calc is optional).
keyPoints: calc() mixes units; spaces required around + and -
min() caps a value from above, max() sets a floor
clamp(min, preferred, max) gives fluid, bounded sizes
Combine rem + vw for accessible fluid typography
Replace many media queries with clamp()
pitfalls: Using pure vw for font-size (no zoom support)
Mixing up min() and max() semantics (min = upper bound)

topics.title: Container Queries
topics.summary: Style components based on the size of their container, not the viewport.
keyPoints: container-type: inline-size marks a parent as a query container
@container (width <= 600px) styles descendants
Components adapt to their slot, not the screen
cqi / cqw units are relative to the container
Use media queries for page-level, container queries for components
pitfalls: Trying to style the container itself inside its own @container rule

Expecting the container to grow with content after inline-size containment

interview.q: What is the difference between media queries and container queries?
interview.a: Media queries depend on the viewport; container queries depend on the size of a specified ancestor container, making components context-aware.

interview.q: What do you need to declare before using @container?
interview.a: An ancestor with container-type (usually inline-size), optionally named with container-name.

interview.q: What are cqw and cqi units?
interview.a: Percentages of the query container's width (cqw) or inline size (cqi), usable for fluid sizing inside a component.
